12eq7j1:388: “Have you raised a crayfish?” — this was the most popular social greeting in the spring of 2026. A month ago, I followed the trend and bought a lightweight server on Alibaba Cloud for 68 yuan, deploying OpenClaw with one click. That cute little crayfish settled into my server, online 24/7, able to control the computer, execute commands, and send messages. And then? Then I realized I had no idea how to “teach” it to do work. This is probably the common confusion of all “crayfish keepers”: OpenClaw gives you an idling engine — it has the ability to do anything, but it doesn’t know what you want it to do. Some people use it to automatically scrape announcements and watch the market for stock picks, some use it to post articles to WeChat Official Accounts with one click, and some use it to handle government and livelihood services. What’s the difference? The difference is that those who actually use it have all learned one thing: writing an “instruction manual” for the AI. Today, I’ll guide you to write one by hand. We’re going to build a Resume Forge Skill — converting your Markdown resume to PDF with one click. Along the way, you don’t need to write complex Agent code — just SKILL.md, combined with OpenClaw’s Skills mechanism.
